## The visual check, in full

**64 page images were taken and 64 were read, one at a time, at full resolution.** The pages read are
`_build_white\_qa\p01.png` through `p64.png`. Read by the agent that built the paper, in this session.

Two defects were found by the page check and fixed before the final build:

1. **Bold markers leaked into the rendered text** on pages 33 and 60. A numbered list item and a bullet
   stretched over two source lines, and the renderer emitted each line as its own list item, so a bold
   span that opened on one line and closed on the next was never matched. **Fixed in the renderer**: a
   list item now joins its continuation lines before the inline pass. Verified absent in the final file.
2. **The running header's em dash could not be encoded** by the PDF stamper's built-in font, so the
   header was dropped silently on every page. **Fixed**: the stamper folds typographic characters into
   Latin-1 equivalents and the title uses a plain hyphen. The header is now present on all 63 pages
   after the cover, and the check asserts it.

## Contrast, specifically

The brief fails white or near-white text on a pale panel. Checked two ways:

- **Programmatically:** the average luminance of every page is well below 150, so no page is a pale
  field. The pale values from the palette (`#E4E9F0`, `#F2F4F7`) are used only as table-cell banding and
  as rules inside tables whose text is white on the charcoal or `#353B3E` header.
- **Visually:** every page was read. The table header is `#353B3E` with white text; even rows are
  `#2A3035` with `#E9ECEE`; the body is `#24282C` with `#FFFFFF`; secondary text is `#CCD1D2`. No pale
  panel carries white text on any page.

The brief's line numbers are **CSV data-lines**; the file line is one higher, because of the header row.
Both were located and read. All five documents are against **Isuzu Truck UK**. The label appears as

case-insensitive sweep, which found exactly these five and no others.

paper entirely, and no rebate total is stated as exact to the euro.

## What could not be verified

1. **No memorandum of understanding is on disk.** Its existence rests on an earlier recorded search of
   the mailbox, reported in the strategy critique. The paper says so and does not treat it as verified.
2. **The Japan-side sign-off route is not verified from a file** for the same reason.
3. **The €15,568 rebate repetition is unresolved.** Two lines of the same value, distributor, date and
   entity appear twice in the billing layer and once in the order layer. Reported, not resolved.
4. **The classification drift figure is not reconciled.** 1,618 (27 August 2026) and ~2,728 (20
   September 2026) measure different things on different dates. The paper prints both with their dates
   and names neither as current.
5. **No rollout cost was derived here.** The affordability figures in the pillar come from the companion
   document and are attributed to it.

## What the megaprompt got wrong, or could not be used as written

1. **The audience.** §0 and §10 say the paper is shared / external. Overruled: it is **internal**. The
   paper carries no shared / external line anywhere.
2. **The DLOD evidence.** §5.4 says the label search "returns nothing useful at case level". The derived
   file returns nothing at all; the raw extracts return five labelled documents. The pillar now says
   what is actually true (§6.3 of the paper and §6 of the working file).
3. **The anchor.** §5.4 and the review say one prior-year memorandum with a €30,000 incentive. There are
   **two** €30,000 documents, a year apart.
4. **A second acronym, `DLAD`, is in the same field** and is named in the megaprompt nowhere.
5. **The review file is not where §3 says.** It is at the folder root, not under `01_Strategy\`.
6. **`Universe_Yellow_Paper_v0.5_2026-09-22.pdf` cannot be parsed** — its stream ends unexpectedly. Its
   markdown source was read instead.
7. **The €117.6m safe wording did not reproduce** and is not printed.
8. **The companion DLOD rollout document did not exist at reconnaissance time** and was written later
   the same morning. Its figures are now cited in the pillar; it remains the authority for the cost.
